newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: ALPINE SKIING-AUSTRIA'S KNAUSS PLANS COMEBACK FOR SLOVENIA.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-AUSTRIA'S KNAUSS PLANS COMEBACK FOR SLOVENIA.

text.p: Nine years after dropping out of the Austrian Alpine skiing team, Bernhard Knauss is planning a World Cup comeback with the Slovenian squad.

Knauss, older brother of Austrian World Cup skier Hans, is due to decide this weekend whether he will rejoin the circuit for the March 8 to 9 races in Shigakogen, Japan, or at the start of next season.
The 31-year-old quit the Austrian squad after a dispute in 1988, before joining the professional ski tour in the United States where his many victories made him a millionaire.
Knauss returned to Europe last summer and decided to give ski racing a final go with the Slovenian team on the FIS and Europacup circuits and surprised even himself with good results.
He is currently third in the overall Europacup giant slalom standings and is guaranteed a starting bib in the discipline's World Cup next season if he holds this position.
Many skiers have managed the jump back to the World Cup through the Europacup.
Austria's only downhill skier to have won races this seasons, Fritz Strobl, returned to the sport's elite by clinching last year's Europacup super-giant slalom title.

Therefore, Knauss may postpone his World Cup return, originally scheduled for Shigakogen, to next winter in order to participate in the Europacup finals in France which take place on the same weekend.
"The snow in Japan is so soft there is little point in racing with a high start number around the 40s," said Knauss. "I wouldn't really stand a chance against the others."
Knauss remains realistic about his chances on the World Cup where he would ski alongside his 26-year-old brother Hans, who is considered Austria's most talented all-rounder.
"I have no illusions. The World Cup is a completely different ball game to the pro-tour," he said.
"I had already given up a return to the World Cup. But then I realized that good technique is something you either have or don't have."

Knauss, whose last appearance in the World Cup dates back to a slalom in St. Anton in December 1988, has had dual nationality for three years but is not the first Austrian skier to compete for another country.
Others to have left the ski-crazed nation's federation include the recently retired five-time overall World Cup champion Marc Girardelli, who recorded all his wins for Luxembourg.

Claudia Riegler, a slalom specialist and winner of three races this season, opted to compete for her mother's country, New Zealand, when the Austrian team required skiers to train in more than one discipline.
Austrian-born Markus Eberle began posting top ten results this season after changing to the German team two years ago.
